decisions.executionNote: Begin a gradual forward pitch and lift with both open grippers, preserving the initial elbow branch; establish a top-down approach.
Finish downward gripper pitch; approach the near-center pepper with the left arm and lion-shaped wooden toy with the right, keeping separate workspaces.
Refine alignment from calibrated head and wrist views, lowering open grippers over the pepper and wooden lion.
The pepper shifted and the right approach appears obstructed. Lift and back off slightly, realigning without closing on uncertain geometry.
Make a shallow final descent with centered objects, then close both grippers. Retention will be checked by lifting and RGB.
Lift both closed grasps clear of the tabletop and inspect whether pepper and lion remain between the jaws.
Lion is visibly retained; carry it above the right basket. Pepper stayed on the table, so reopen and retry lower at its new centered position.
Replan the interrupted basket approach with smaller forward increments and reduced height; left gripper descends around the pepper without lateral sweeping.
Close the left gripper lower around the pepper. Move the retained lion into the red basket opening and release it there.
Release the lion at the currently reachable point inside the red basket and retract. Close then test-lift the pepper without lateral motion.
Carry the retained pepper toward the white basket. Approach the near-right watch with the now empty right gripper.
Advance the pepper above the white basket with modest forward finger tilt to retain reach margin; lower the right gripper around the watch.
Release pepper inside the white basket and retract; close on the right watch and lift to verify retention.
The right watch remained on the table. Reopen and approach lower; concurrently align the left gripper with the leftmost watch.
Center the watch bands between the jaws, close at the reachable table-contact height, then lift both for a visual grasp check.
Carry the visibly retained left watch to the blue basket while retrying the smaller right watch at its shifted position.
Back the left watch away from the basket lip and lift for clearance after the guard interruption. Close and test-lift the recentered right watch.
Neither watch is securely retained. Target the solid case of the right watch rather than its hollow band, and approach the remaining wooden toy with the left gripper.
Lift the right watch without sideways motion to check retention. Center and close the left jaws on the wooden toy, then lift.
Stage the wooden toy near the center boundary for a non-crossing right-arm pickup. Retry the right watch with the jaws centered farther toward its solid case.
Correct right-watch case alignment laterally before closing. The wooden toy slipped during staging; reopen and move back above its visible location.
Test the right watch grasp with a straight lift, while lowering and closing more deeply around the staged wooden toy.
Both objects now appear retained. Carry the watch toward the middle basket, keeping the left wooden toy low and back from the right arm's route.
Advance the retained watch over the blue basket with forward finger tilt and smaller increments. Keep the empty left arm stationary and separated.
Release the watch into the middle basket, then retract the right arm. Approach the displaced left watch without crossing the arms.
Align the left jaws around the displaced watch case at table height, while approaching the remaining right-side pepper.
Grip the near side of the left watch clear of the basket wall. Lift and recenter above the pepper after it rolled, then approach vertically.
Narrow the left opening to approach the watch case near the basket lip. Reposition the right gripper higher before centering over the rolled pepper.
Retreat from the obstructing basket wall and approach the central watch from the left. Lower around the recentered right pepper and close.
Lower the left jaws at the near case of the central watch, remaining on the left side. Lift and carry the pepper inward within the right workspace.
Close on the central watch's near case and lift. Carry the retained pepper toward a center-boundary staging point, behind and separated from the left arm.
Place the retained central watch above the blue basket using a forward tilt. Retract the right arm to inspect where the pepper slipped during staging.
Lift and back off to clear the blue basket lip before any further insertion. Reapproach the pepper at its newly observed position.
Replan with a tiny initial adjustment to regain joint-target continuity, then gradually back away and lift from the obstruction; approach the pepper with the right arm.
Restore a vertical left grasp approach to the watch case in front of the blue basket. Center lower around the pepper and close the right gripper.
Close the left gripper and test-lift the watch vertically. Lift the pepper slowly, avoiding lateral acceleration that previously caused slipping.
Lift and tilt the tentative left watch grasp for basket clearance. Reopen the right gripper and approach the pepper more deeply to reduce slipping.
Recenter the pepper between the right pads before closing. The watch slipped clear of the basket lip; reapproach its near case vertically.
Align directly with the visible watch face rather than its hollow band. Make a lower, slightly rearward pepper grasp to engage more of the finger pads.
Close at the current watch alignment and lift slowly. Test the deeper pepper grasp with a straight, low-acceleration lift.
Raise the retained watch fully above the basket rim before advancing. Move the pepper slowly inward while maintaining a closed grip and separate arm paths.
Correct the rejected tensor without compensating for motion. Advance the retained watch high over the blue basket and approach the pepper more deeply.
Release the watch over the blue basket, then withdraw. Lift the right gripper fully before moving sideways above the displaced pepper.
The second watch is visible inside the blue basket. Approach the last watch from its near side; center the pepper while high, then descend straight down.
Close around the near watch band without advancing into the basket. Make a centered, deeper pepper grasp and a small straight lift.
Withdraw and lift the watch clear of the basket wall. Test a very slow, low-height pepper transfer to limit slipping.
Continue the pepper's slow low transfer while it remains visibly between the pads. Reapproach the watch's near strap with a narrower opening to clear the basket.
Try drawing the last watch away from the obstructing basket by its near strap. Continue the stable low pepper transfer toward the center boundary.
Regrasp the pepper lower after the slip. Use the narrow closed left fingers to approach the watch opening, aiming to draw it away from the basket before a normal grasp.
Lower the narrow left fingers into the watch opening. Lift clear and recenter the right jaws around the pepper rather than sweeping it with a low finger.
Withdraw from the basket obstruction and rotate the left grasp axis for a narrower approach. Reorient the right jaws across the pepper's shorter dimension before retrying.
Finish the perpendicular grasp orientations and descend gradually: left toward the watch's near strap, right across the pepper's short axis.
Refine alignment in the rotated wrist views, close across the watch and pepper, then make small test lifts while retreating from the basket wall.
Transport the pepper inward with the improved perpendicular grasp. Leave the obstructed watch for now and approach the remaining wooden toy with the left arm.
Center and close on the toy's body in the rotated left view. Bring the visibly retained pepper to the right side of the center staging boundary.
Set the pepper down at the center staging boundary and retract the right arm. Lift the wooden toy toward the left to verify and maintain separation.
Move the retained wooden toy to a separate center-boundary staging point ahead of the pepper; retract the right arm fully to preserve separation.
Release the staged toy and withdraw the left arm rearward. Approach it with the right arm while the left prepares to pick the staged pepper without crossing the arm bases.
Approach the separated staging points: left pepper behind, right wooden toy ahead. Use slight inward fingertip tilts while keeping each EE on its own side.
The staging approaches interfered. Replan from observed poses, separate both wrists, and restore orientations gradually before sequential pickups.
Pick up the staged pepper sequentially with the left arm; keep the right wrist stationary and clear until this pickup is complete.
Close the centered left grip, lift the staged pepper, and retreat leftward while keeping the right arm clear.
Carry the retained pepper high toward the left basket. After the left wrist clears the center, approach the staged wooden toy with the right arm.
Advance the pepper over the white basket with forward finger tilt. Refine the right toy approach using a small inward fingertip tilt, keeping the EE in the right workspace.
Release the second pepper into the white basket and retract. Close on the staged wooden toy and lift it toward the right workspace for a retention check.
Both peppers are now in the white basket. Reapproach the last watch's near strap from in front of the rim, and lower the right toy grasp more deeply at its current position.
Close and lift the deeper right toy grasp. Refine the left grip onto the near strap, then withdraw and lift away from the basket.
Carry the visibly retained wooden toy high toward the red basket. Align the narrower left opening with the remaining watch case, approaching slowly near the rim.
The toy slipped in transit; return above it. Change the last-watch approach to forward-tilted fingertips with the wrist farther back, avoiding the obstructing basket housing contact.
Lower the tilted left fingers onto the watch case and close without advancing the housing into the baskets. Reorient the right grasp across the toy's body while remaining above it.
Lift and withdraw the tentative watch grasp clear of the rim. Lower the right jaws across the wooden toy's body and close before testing retention.
Compensate for the tilted left fingertips with a lower watch approach, keeping the wrist behind the baskets. Slowly lift and carry the new right toy grasp outward.
Make a small final watch-case alignment, close and test-lift. Continue the stable right wooden-toy carry toward the red basket with moderate increments.
The watch is now visibly caught by its strap; lift it well above the rim before transfer. Reopen and recenter above the toy where it slipped nearer the red basket.
Carry the retained last watch above the blue basket with rim clearance. Recenter and close the right jaws around the wooden toy's broad base.
Release the last watch inside the middle basket and withdraw the left arm. Test-lift the right toy grasp gently before the final basket transfer.
All watches appear inside the middle basket. Retreat the left arm toward its reset corridor; reopen and lower the right grasp more deeply around the remaining wooden toy.
